note: v1: first version of 'Cross Purposes' (Odd Hours t7), GENTLE GIANT / ZAPPA COUNTERPOINT, 100 bpm, 161 s, 80 bars, generator compose/chirpers2/src/chirpers2-t7.py. A nine-note chromatic SUBJECT over 7/8 + 5/8 (D F A G# E | G Eb F# D) and its inversion drive seven sections: STATEMENT (hocketed note by note across marimba / flute / muted trumpet / guitar, rotation turning; unison; inverted low under hocketed fragments), FUGUE (sax, trumpet at A, guitar inverted, bass; wurli a chord per bar), BLACK PAGE (whole-band rhythmic unison in 11 13 9 15 11 13 7 17 sixteenths, toms on every hit), CROSS PURPOSES (horns cycling the subject's 7-bar against a 4/4 figure, subject augmented in the bass, ride bell on the 7), TRADES (sax and trumpet trade bars over a 7 5 6 9 wheel, walking bass), STRETTO (entries every two eighths in all seven voices), CODA (augmentation, then the subject's pitch set stacked one hocketed note an eighth). Kit grouping flips bar by bar. Song-local marimba (additive bars). compscore seed 0: 79.78 (structure, master, length, distinct 100; variety 84.3, recurrence 56.0, rhythm 55.8, spectrum 72.2, cohesion 56.3; master rms -17.8, crest 13.2). styles.md, motifs.md, sounds.md rows added; titled.
next: Recurrence 56: a RITORNELLO (the unison subject returning between sections, varied each time); rhythm 55.8; listen for balance (flute/marimba vs horns), the trades' improvised lines, and the black page's precision.

note: v2: CONTRAST. compscore's recurrence was over its band (share 0.787 > 0.7: the sections resembled each other too much) and variety's level range only 5.1 dB, so the TRADES become a hushed chamber episode after the loud black page and cross purposes: the kit drops to the hat pedal's chick on each group start, one soft wurli chord a bar, the soloists quiet over the walking bass, and a master gain lane AFTER the glue (so it is not squashed back) lowers it 6 dB until the last wheel turn wakes into the stretto. Seeds 0/11: 79.78 / 80.90 -> 86.59 / 86.05; recurrence share 0.79 -> 0.68 (in band), level range 5.1 -> 9.9 dB, variety 84 -> 92. Tried within the round: a ride on the group starts made the quiet section ride-dominated (4-16 kHz -16 -> -5 dB of its energy; spectrum 72 -> 54, cohesion 56 -> 33) and velocity alone did not lower its level (the glue made it up). Spectrum (61) and cohesion (46) are still below v1's 72 / 56 (worst band: the low end).
next: Spectrum/cohesion: the low end (worst band 1) and the quiet section's thinness; rhythm 55.8 (all on the eighth grid: a passage of triplets or quintuplets?); listen for balance.

Every bar still differs from the one before, and the solos now argue with the subject like the rest of the piece. note: v5: I wrote two new voices into the argument. THE CLOCK: a toy piano ticking every five sixteenths through the fugue and cross purposes, cycling the subject's pitches two octaves up with an accent every fourth tick. It is a gear that turns against every meter and lands somewhere new in each bar, so cross purposes now argues three against five against seven (flute/marimba/guitar triplets, the clock's fives, the horns' sevens). THE SUB FLOOR (answering chirper-one's note that the lows sat 11-17 dB under the album at 38-71 Hz, and transforming their t2 'low end under the fretless'): a sine doubles the whole bass line an octave down in the loud sections, never under D1, and drops out for the hushed trades so the hush stays a hush. Seeds 0/11: 85.99 / 84.69 -> 89.48 / 87.63; spectrum 65 -> 87, cohesion 57 -> 76, barvariety 78 / 71 -> 91 / 76 (anchor 0.47 -> 0.49). A first take with the clock everywhere was wallpaper: 19 dB under the mix, and it flattened the sections' densities (variety -7); focusing it on two sections, 8 dB louder, made it a voice. Rhythm is still 55.8 (off-grid share 0.0). sounds.md and motifs.md rows added.
next: Rhythm: off-grid share 0.0 even with triplets and the 5-clock (the eighth pulse dominates): swing the hushed trades (walking bass on quarters), or a whole section in a triplet/quintuplet pulse; a new section? (a chorale or a solo cadenza); listen for the clock's balance.

note: v6 (judgment keep, compscore -3.7; Harry: compscore is a guardrail): I rewrote the hushed TRADES as a SWINGING BRUSH TRIO, the piece's one turn into chamber jazz. The sax and muted trumpet's motivic bars now swing (off-beat eighths at 0.62 of the beat, mapped piecewise so sixteenth figures keep their order); the bass walks on the quarters (chord tones up the bar, a chromatic approach into the next root, a half-beat pickup in odd bars); the wurli comps on the 'and'; and the kit is chirper-two's physical-layer BRUSHES (borrowed from t4: a sweep through each bar, taps on alternate beats) under a soft ride with its swung skip. The last wheel turn still wakes straight, with sticks, into the stretto. Balance took three takes: at first the brushes and the borrowed felt kick WERE the section (drums -26 dB vs mix -25; 30-60 Hz +21 dB, 4-16 kHz +20 dB); now no kick, sweeps -20 dB, taps -14 dB, ride 20 velocities lower (trades -27.8 dB, lows back to -75 dB). Seeds 0/11: v5 89.70 / 87.85 -> 85.46 / 84.52. The cost is mostly RECURRENCE (share 0.75, over its 0.7 band: in spectrum/chroma terms the swung trades now resemble another section, though swing vs straight is the audible difference), then spectrum 87 -> 81 and cohesion 82 -> 65; barvariety s11 76 -> 86. Before/after shared with Harry; v5 is one revert away if the straight hush is preferred.
